A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, algorithms, figures, references, and Appendices A–E are readable and support a complete comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B report original synthetic experiments on contextual bandits and preference learning, including sampling comparisons and KL-regularization sensitivity.

after.justification: Appendix B retains both original synthetic experiments and their results in Figures 1–2.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain reference-policy sampling, reward estimation, intermediate-policy sampling, and refitting on pooled data. TMPS and TMPS-PF are new names for the existing procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic contextual-bandit and Bradley–Terry preference-learning tasks, using five actions and ten-dimensional linear rewards. Moving the experiments to Appendix B does not change coverage.

E2.justification: Offline sampling from the reference policy remains the experimental comparator for mixed-policy sampling in both tasks. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The reported data generation, sample-size range, m = n allocation, suboptimality metric, and regularization settings are retained. V2 newly identifies the reference policy as uniform, but does not establish that the experimental setting changed.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the sampling-strategy comparison and sensitivity analysis over the same five regularization values. No additional ablation, robustness test, or case study appears.

E5.justification: Both report ten repetitions and error bars described as standard variation. The reporting practice and plotted uncertainty are unchanged.

E6.justification: All four experimental panels retain identical plotted results and uncertainty bars. V1 Figure 1 matches v2 Figure 2, and v1 Figure 2 matches v2 Figure 1; the findings about mixed sampling and regularization are unchanged.

T1.justification: V1's shared coverage definition is replaced by separate bandit and preference definitions: v2 Definition 3.5 removes context offsets, while Definition 4.5 uses variance and an existential offset. Lower-bound Theorems 3.1/4.3 become 3.6/4.6, changing epsilon in (0,1) and eta > 0 to epsilon in (0,1/256) and eta > 4, and replacing O(1) coverage with O(N_R(epsilon)). Appendices C.1, D.1, and Lemma D.1 also revise substantive KL-divergence calculations.

C1.justification: The headline contributions remain sharp O(1/epsilon) sample complexity for both feedback settings and two-stage learning with additive data-coverage dependence. V2 explicitly highlights matching lower bounds already represented by v1's lower- and upper-bound results.

C2.justification: V2 adds feature-space interpretations of coverage and explains preference coverage through relative reward errors. It removes the blanket D² ≤ C_GL comparison and stops presenting local coverage as simply weaker than data coverage. The conclusion additionally identifies additive dependence under global-policy coverage as an open direction.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly states that the experimental reference policy is uniform random. This supplies a reproducibility detail missing from v1 without demonstrating a changed implementation.

R1.justification: V2 adds a focused comparison with Lan (2023), distinguishing optimization assumptions from sample-based exploration analysis. It also adds contextual-bandit and G-optimal-design references while pruning several dueling-bandit and RLHF citations; the overall research positioning remains similar.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: related work becomes Section 2, preliminaries are distributed into task-specific setups, and experiments move entirely to Appendix B. The abstract and introduction are rewritten, and the main upper-bound explanation is expanded into a two-part walkthrough.

P2.justification: The existing figures are grouped together in Appendix B and exchange numbers. Their panels, axes, legends, and error bars are retained. Algorithm captions gain acronyms, with accompanying placement and page-layout changes.

improvement.justification: V2 makes useful corrections to lower-bound conditions and identifiable proof steps in Appendices C.1 and D.2, improves the explanation of the analysis, and discloses the uniform experimental reference policy. These provide a limited quality gain with unchanged empirical evidence. The revised coverage assumptions are inconsistently referenced: Theorem 4.7 and Lemma D.5 cite Definition 3.5, while the latter's proof invokes Definition 4.5, limiting confidence in a broader theoretical improvement.
